we developed a novel theoretical framework to study the fission process and we applied our theory to a number of fission reactions and compared our results with the available experimental data.

we have obtained the analytical expressions of the total kinetic energy distributions of fission fragments and the total kinetic energy distribution of the light fragment in fission process of 232Th and 236U.

the asymptotic expansion of the fission process in terms of the fluctuation strength of the fission barrier is possible and that the mean kinetic energy of the fission fragment and the variance of kinetic energy are obtained by the asymptotic expansion.

a study of the asymptotic expansion of the solution of the Fokkr-Planck equation.
the fission process and the fission fragment distribution.
the study of the statistical properties of the fission process and the application of these properties to the calculation of the average values of the total kinetic energy of fission fragments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fission process is well described by the present model.

the fission process is well described by the Fokker--Planck equation, but the present theory does not give a complete description of the fission process, since it does not take into account the fluctuation in the number of neutrons emitted in fission.
the fission process is not a stochastic process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mean kinetic energy and the variance of total kinetic energy are well described by our theory.
the fission fragments are not independent and that the total kinetic energies are not additive.
, the asymptotic expansion of the fission process in terms of the fluctuation strength is very useful for describing the fission process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fission process can be understood in terms of the mean field and the fluctuating field, and the fluctuation plays the most important role.
the fluctuation in the fission barrier is the most important source of the variance in the fission fragment kinetic energies.
the fission process is a non-Markovian process, and that the Fokker–Planck equation is a non-Marcovian process.
